title: Trace a complex ELS API question
question: When requesting indicator data, which geography and date filters can a client plan, and what evidence limits apply to an answer?

worked_answer.dates: The reviewed data route records `time` as latest, earliest, all, one date or a comma-separated inclusive range. `timeNearest` selects none, latest, earliest or any when a date falls outside an indicator's range. The recorded defaults are latest and none.
worked_answer.geography: The reviewed data route records `geo` as one or more comma-separated geography-level keys or GSS codes, `geoExtent` as a parent GSS code, and `geoCluster` as a statistical cluster. Their recorded defaults are all. A separate `/api/v1/geo/lookup/{code}` route takes a GSS code and is described as returning one GeoJSON feature; it has no query parameters in this review.
worked_answer.conflicts: The wiki says the data route's `hasGeo` default is all, while the pinned application review records any. The wiki also contradicts itself about the `includeNames` name/default; the reviewed route accepts `includeNames` and records true. Keep those differences visible rather than choosing a live truth.
worked_answer.limits: This is a frozen wiki snapshot and bounded static source review, not a live check. The measure parameter's allowed values and interactions are undocumented, and complete response/error schemas are absent. The bundle cannot establish current behaviour or a safe executable request.
